pages.says: Ukraine says its sea drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury in Benghazi harbour, which carries the naval war 2,000km from the Black Sea into Libya, a country that is not part of it.
pages.weakest: "On Hacker News the story drew one comment."

pages.says: India pledged Nepal's new prime minister nearly $1.6 billion, mostly loans and only about $400 million in grants, and both sides left the disputed border off the table.
pages.weakest: "Hormuz: at least three ships were hit by projectiles over the weekend..."

pages.says: Singapore and China signed a record 29 agreements at their yearly council, but most are memorandums of intent; the concrete wins are Hainan poultry and eggs and a few yuan-finance steps.
pages.weakest: The Chatter box: "No forum thread on the JCBC had formed by Tuesday morning..."

pages.says: A hand-built wheel comes down to choosing a hub, spokes, rims and a builder; Chris King hubs carry a lifetime warranty, Singapore builders charge S$120-140 to lace a pair, and humid weather is what kills brass nipples.
pages.weakest: "Industry Nine's Hydra2, launched in March 2025, reaches 870 points, against 690 before."

pages.says: Nvidia took Jensen Huang back eleven days after he resigned, saying the US government told it he posed no security risk, and critics from both parties in Congress objected.
pages.weakest: "Two of the loudest Republican critics, Cornyn and Bacon, are leaving Congress."

pages.says: Dragos planted bait in prompts and showed that three AI hosting firms had been breached and that 'zero retention' prompts still leaked; OpenRouter then dropped 125 endpoints.
pages.weakest: "Two releases this week show both sides of that. Z.ai announced GLM-5.4..."
pages.reason: Partway through, the story breaks off for two model releases (GLM-5.4, Nari's Qwen build) that have nothing to do with the leak, and the method only gets explained afterwards. Cut the model detour or move it to a brief, and explain the bait method straight after the opening.
pages.fixed: Bait method moved to the first paragraph; GLM-5.4 and NariQ moved to briefs.

pages.says: Google's Android-only Pixel Tag tracker sells here for S$44.99 and reviews well, but it has no keyring hole and depends on how many Android phones are nearby.
pages.weakest: "The tag went on sale less than a month before Engadget's review"

pages.says: Roger W. Smith marked his firm's 25th year with the Series Seven, a tourbillon with an annual calendar that he will make only once or twice a year, and SJX finds its tourbillon underwhelming.
pages.weakest: "Seiko: a green-dial Marinemaster 1968 Heritage, HBF003, 900 pieces at €3,800..."

pages.says: The Stallone biopic I Play Rocky came second on its first wide weekend with $9.3m after critics and audiences praised it.
pages.weakest: The Chatter box, which repeats the 98 per cent audience score and the 1,788 per cent/nineteen-fold jump already given above.
pages.reason: The page gives the same numbers again and again: the 1,788 per cent jump appears three times, the 98 per cent audience score three times, and the seven-cinema opening twice. Say each figure once, and use the space for something new.
pages.fixed: Each figure now stated once; Chatter rewritten to the audience scores; new release-strategy material.

pages.says: A large Chinese study links compulsive, heavy short-video use in teenagers to more suicidal thoughts and self-harm, though pupils who dropped the habit stopped adding to that risk.
pages.weakest: "What a parent can take from it is narrow but useful..."
pages.reason: The page says it twice. The 'what a parent can take' paragraph repeats points from the earlier paragraphs. Merge them into one practical paragraph that tells a parent what to look for.
pages.fixed: The parent's takeaway and the exit finding merged into one practical paragraph.

pages.says: PSLE results come out at 11am and families get six days to rank six schools; the page explains how scores map to posting groups and tie-breaks and how to choose safely.
pages.weakest: The Chatter box, which only repeats MOE's advice from the paragraph above

pages.says: Huang's reinstatement lifted the S&P 500 4.7 per cent and took the fear gauge down, but the desk says the Fed is still tightening.
pages.weakest: "Lean: firmer; a NAV back under US$172.97 on 1 December proves it wrong."
pages.reason: The page assumes I know 'the four', 'No. 166's leans' and the desk's running calls and never explains them. It also retells the Nvidia story from p7. Open with what the rally means for an ordinary fund holder, say in one line what the four are and why they are tracked, and tie the Sceptic box clearly to the rally or cut it.
pages.fixed: Lede rewritten for a fund holder; one-line explanation of the four instruments and the leans; Sceptic tied to the rally.

pages.says: Analysts keep raising S&P 500 profit forecasts while share prices have fallen, so the whole drop has come from investors paying less for each dollar of earnings.
pages.weakest: The Call box opening sentence

pages.says: A cryptic clue pairs a definition with wordplay, and this October a University of Texas program called Darmok solved the Times championship final faster than its youngest-ever human winner.
pages.weakest: "'A human solver brings one mind and a pencil,' Chatterjee told his university."

pages.says: Cryptic solvers learn from daily blog post-mortems, setters write under several pen-names, and the kit is a few subscriptions and dictionaries.
pages.weakest: Headline: "Chambers Dictionary, last revised in 2014, still rules the setters' shelf"
pages.reason: The headline and standfirst are about Chambers and subscription prices, but the page is about blogs and pen-names. The Times £1 offer is priced here and again on p18. Retitle the page for its real subject and leave the prices to p18.
pages.fixed: Retitled to blogs and pen-names; subscription prices moved to p18; new paragraph on the setters' guild.

pages.says: Getting into cryptics costs about £10 and a commissioned puzzle a few hundred pounds, in a month when Don Manley retired from the FT and the Independent's cryptic moved to The i Paper.
pages.weakest: The Sceptic box on America and cricket
pages.reason: The headline is about Don Manley's farewell, but the page is a costs-and-first-steps guide. Its Sceptic box goes back to Darmok and America instead of arguing against the costs. Lead with the price path and make the box a real case against spending.
pages.fixed: Opens on the price path; Manley and the Independent as the why; Sceptic now argues against spending.

pages.says: In a 40-week trial, people on tirzepatide who lifted weights three times a week lost as much weight as those who did not but kept more muscle and got stronger.
pages.weakest: "The programme ran in five eight-week blocks..."

pages.says: A booking calendar for Singapore and the region, led by Disney On Ice in March, with general sale at 10am tomorrow, and the Final Fantasy exhibition in Tokyo from January.
pages.weakest: "Ticketmaster refused this desk, so live availability is unconfirmed."

pages.says: British Hainan has reopened in a Tiong Bahru coffeeshop with its pork chop at S$17.90; Stamford Social and a second MUTED Gelato are new, but there are too few reviews to judge them yet.
pages.weakest: The Honest Ledger: "MUTED's Joo Chiat shop opened before October, outside this month."

pages.says: Japan has shortlisted gengoka, 'putting it into words', as a buzzword of the year, a sign that a culture built on sensing what goes unsaid now prizes saying it plainly.
pages.weakest: "...the world's fourth-largest economy and Singapore's fifth-largest source of investment and tourists alike."

pages.says: Surveys show Japanese adults shifting toward saying things outright, and the page puts this down to job-hopping and AI wearing away the shared context that reading the air depended on.
pages.weakest: "Chat software replaced half the room anyway."

pages.says: Gengoka responds to the old 'air' Yamamoto warned about, but it moves the cost of being understood onto the individual, and only the long-run surveys will show whether it is a real change or a fad.
pages.weakest: "A second thread, from May 2025, ran on the same nerve..."
